fix: Label S = 8/16 and the 300/1,000 cut points as budget conventions in the Candidates row of RECIPES_AND_TUNING.md §4.2 (line 785) and at SOBOL_SIZES (turbotab/core/models/tuning.py:101), and scope the 'standard can never lose' guarantee to the inner loss; settling the open §4.6 item (the small-sample standard as a second standard candidate from 300) would address the 5-of-8-cells finding.

It never claims that 8 or 16 candidates give settings that predict at least as well as the standard on new data. fix: No behavior change. Make the known-truth test in test_explore_3_selection.py able to fail (q below the true count, B = 50, correlated predictors), and correct the stability_q docstring (turbotab/core/models/variable_selection.py:281-283) to say the bound is at most one.
evidence: Both referees and the audit confirm that q = floor(sqrt(0.2p)) gives q^2/(0.2p) <= 1, and that Shah & Samworth carry the M&B bound over to complementary pairs under its assumptions. The inventory's objections fail on all three points. For p < 5, q = 1, so each half selects one column, the selection proportions sum to 1, at most one column can reach tau = 0.6, and V <= 1 holds deterministically. LARS on a 0/1 outcome is a valid base procedure. Lifting columns to terms cannot make false terms outnumber false columns. The only weakness is a test that cannot fail.

fix: Restore the verbatim Keogh quote in INTERVAL_REFUSALS (turbotab/core/methods/calibration.py:687-688: 'when performing regression calibration', not 'RC'). Where the docs read as 'must' (MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 7, line 83; line 237 'implies'), say the whole-chain bootstrap is the app's chosen route and that a stacked-estimating-equation sandwich is also valid (Keogh et al. 2020 §6.1.2).
evidence: The app refuses only model_based and rubin_only. Both are too narrow, and the referees and the audit agree. The refusal says 'Its interval comes from a bootstrap over the whole chain', which describes the app's route without claiming it is the only valid one. No stacked sandwich is offered or refused, so no valid estimate is withheld, and the referees' 'must' objection hits only the inventory's wording. The PSU branch is Rao & Wu's rescaling bootstrap (n_h - 1 draws, weights times n_h/(n_h - 1); calibration.py:560-583), so two-PSU strata are not under-dispersed. fix: Label the two-value rule as TurboTab's convention in read_features (turbotab/core/methods/subgroups.py:216-217). In the k-means/mixture category refusal (subgroups.py:913-929), give a two-valued numeric column a 'Read it as an amount (0/1)' exit (numeric=[...]), as the ambiguous 3-10-value columns get, and stop citing Huang's arbitrary-coding reason for a single 0/1 column. evidence: Referee B is right that reading binaries as nominal is the usual convention for mixed-type data (Gower; Hennig & Liao). Referee A is right that the number of values observed does not fix the measurement level. A single 0/1 column has one non-arbitrary coding, so the refusal's Huang reason does not apply to it. fix: In turbotab/core/methods/trials.py:57-58 and the interval line built from df at :1365-1366, cite Li & Redden 2015 only for K - 2 with two arms and no covariates, and label counting only the within-cluster-constant terms as the app's between-within convention. With few clusters, also count individual-level covariates whose variance is mostly between clusters, or use a Satterthwaite (Bell-McCaffrey) df.
evidence: Li & Redden used K - 2 with no covariates and wrote that adding covariates 'will change ... the degrees of freedom' (the audit verified this), so the cluster-level-terms rule is the app's own extension presented under their name. My simulation (Kauermann-Carroll-corrected sandwich, null arm effect, 3,000 reps, MC SE about 0.004): t on K minus the cluster-level terms is nominal when covariates vary mainly within clusters (0.051-0.055 at K = 8-10, covariate ICC 0-0.3). It is anti-conservative when covariates are mostly between-cluster but not constant: 0.068 at K = 10 with four covariates at ICC 0.5, and 0.078 at K = 8 with ICC 0.8. So referee B's 'sensible extension' holds in the main regime, and referee A's worry holds at the edge.

fix: Add a test that checks the averaged curve under a logged and a spline component against hand computation (test_substitution.py covers only the linear case). Optionally write 'the all-components model's coefficient contrast is not defined on logged components' at turbotab/core/methods/exposure_form.py:1015-1016.
evidence: Referee B and the audit derive the label. With b*f(x) nonlinear, each person's effect b[f(x +/- k) - f(x)] depends on k and on intake, so each point is an average. methods/substitution.py:substitution_curve averages over the rows on support at each k and stops when the on-support share drops below min_support, which answers referee A's feasibility point ('the rows the curve reads'). Referee A read 'all-components contrast' as any reallocation. In the app it means the all-components model's coefficient difference, which has no per-kcal meaning on logged components.

fix: Add the row-accounting test the audit asks for (a blank in a Missing-level column, in an unsettled role and in a settled numeric predictor, each checked against the flow's counts) at turbotab/core/stages/rows.py:1441-1451 and cohort_inputs (:1459).
evidence: Both referees' objections fail on the code. Rows with a blank outcome are dropped earlier, at the 'outcome_measured' step (rows.py:1362), and the exposure is among predictor_columns (readings.py:1491), so 'only predictors' is the right scope for this step. Under inference, blanks kept as a level are blocked as the missing-indicator method, with Groenwold et al. 2012's caution (decisions.py:4850-4870). They are kept only with an attestation that a blank means not asked or that the covariates are a trial's baseline ones, which is exactly where Groenwold calls the method valid. Under Predict a Missing level is sound.

fix: In identifier_values (turbotab/core/recognizers.py:1440-1467), phrase the reasons as readings ('reads as a category's labels'), label ID_MIN_UNITS = 3 and FEW_UNITS = 10 as conventions, and send up to 10 repeating digit-free word labels to 'few' (asked) rather than 'never', so a small study that codes subjects by name is asked.
evidence: The recognizer is a role heuristic. A 'never' verdict keeps the column as a low-confidence predictor the user can override (rows.py:507-511), and it neither grants nor refuses clustered intervals. The referees' main objection, that 11 to 30 clusters give anti-conservative CR1 intervals, does not apply: clustered rows get CR2 with Bell-McCaffrey df and a concern below 30 clusters (models/inference.py:11, 46, 644). What remains is that the 3/10 cuts and the digit-free-word rule are shown as facts ('a category's labels, not units') although they are conventions, and they can misread a small study whose subjects are named.

fix: Reword the soundness text at turbotab/core/stages/explore.py:745-746 to match what the routed question delivers ('multiple imputation fills blanks given the analysis variables, so the group is in its model only when it is in the analysis; complete cases state their assumption'), or let MI take the group column as an auxiliary variable when this finding fires.
evidence: The audit's point holds, and the referees' in part. The imputation model holds the analysis variables, the outcome, energy and the design (methods/missing.py:6-16), with no path for auxiliary variables. The group candidates are any non-target column named like a sociodemographic group (explore.py:391), so a group that is not a predictor never enters the imputation model the lever promises. The 'complete cases states its assumption' half is right: it does not call complete cases unsound. MI is ranked first under inference anyway, so the main regime, where the group is already a covariate, is unaffected.

fix: Reword DESIGN['why'] at turbotab/core/teaching/content.py:404-407: 'in a randomized trial adjustment is for precision, not confounding, and the effects reported are marginal (standardized); a case-control sample cannot give prevalence or absolute risk without its sampling fractions; individually matched sets are analyzed within each set'.
evidence: Both referees and the audit are right on two points. 'Only sharpens precision' fails for conditional odds and hazard ratios, which are non-collapsible, as the app's own term at content.py:1393 says. A case-control sample with known sampling fractions does give absolute risk. The app's own trial core standardizes to marginal risks and its case-control core handles frequency matching separately, so its analyses agree with the card, but the teaching sentence states a general rule a user could carry elsewhere. The trial designs are 'Not available yet', so the card only explains for now.
